recipes.name: Dad's Breakfast Pizza
ingredients_raw: 2 (12 ounce) cans refrigerated biscuits (10 biscuits per can)
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly spray a 9x12-inch baking sheet with cooking spray.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until the bacon is browned and crisp, about 10 minutes. Remove bacon pieces with a slotted spoon, and drain on paper towels.

Open up the cans of biscuits, separate the biscuits, and arrange onto the prepared baking sheet so they touch. Press the biscuit dough down to seal them together into a crust that covers the baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until the crust is slightly cooked and very lightly browned, about 5 minutes. Do not overbake. Remove from oven.

Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until the foam disappears. Beat the eggs in a bowl, and pour the eggs into the hot skillet. Use a spatula to lift and gently stir the eggs just until set, but still moist, 3 to 4 minutes. Arrange the lightly scrambled eggs on the semi-baked biscuit crust. Top with the cooked bacon, onion, and green pepper; spread the Cheddar cheese all over the pizza. Season to taste with salt and black pepper.
Return to oven, and bake on the top rack until the cheese is melted and bubbling and has begun to brown, about 10 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Dad's Breakfast Pizza
raw_recipe.description: This breakfast pizza, made with refrigerated biscuit dough, is topped with eggs, bacon, and Cheddar cheese.

video.description: Celebrate with a Father's Day breakfast pizza!

review.reviewBody: This is one of our favorite breakfasts. I like it because it's so simple and the family likes it because they get bacon and eggs on a pizza. This works with pretty much anything you want to throw on it and if you have crescent roll dough, that works for a good "crust", too. Just lay it out on the baking sheet like the recipe states, pinching together the seams, and bake for 12-15 minutes. My husband and kids like their breakfast pizza with bacon AND sausage but I like mine with a mix of veggies, like red pepper, red onion, mushrooms, black olives and jalapenos! This recipe is always a winner, no matter what you want to put on it AND if you coupon, it costs you next to nothing for the biscuits/crescent rolls. NOTE: Very important. If you have cranky pans, you might want to squirt a little non stick spray on your pans before you lay out your dough, otherwise you might have an issue getting your pizza out of your pan. I learned this the hard way.

I made this with my 4 year old granddaughter. We used a 10 inch Pyrex pie pan, 6 biscuits, and 6 eggs. We made it to our taste with a layer of cheese, then scrambled eggs very soft set, bacon, and shredded cheese. Topped it with snipped chives when it was out of the oven. I did both bakes on the middle shelf at 400. I think next time I will pat the biscuits thinner and do the first bake longer. I would prefer the crust less doughy. Kids and adults were very happy and I can see lots of variations in the future. It will serve 4 adults.

i love this recipe! but it seemed a bit too dry for our taste, so i read the reviews and used a white sauce, biscuit gravy, put on the semi-cooked biscuits, then topped with bacon, cooked onions, scrambled eggs and shredded cheddar cheese. what a great way to start the day.. i also cooked the "crust " the night before, as suggested by cook, and saves time and prep in the AM. thanx for a great new breakfast fave!

Biscuits! What a great idea for the crust. Of course, any pre-prepared dough would work and be a time saver. Sausage, ham, prosciutto are good bacon substitutes if bacon just isn't your thing...which I just can't imagine.... you really want a soft scramble on the eggs or they will be like eating flubber after being in the oven. If you want whole eggs, you will have to add some sort of sauce to the dough, such as a hollandaise. Sprinkle the onion, pepper, meat, and cheese on top of the sauce, then break whole eggs on top, making a small well for each egg, before baking.

For a gluten free option, preshredded hashbrowns, thawed with butter, pressed into a pizza pan and baked for about 20 min at 400 degrees works great! Season the eggs....I used parsley, cayenne, salt and pepper and sharp cheddar cheese.

This was great! I precooked the bacon, scrambled the eggs and partially baked the ‘crust’ the night before an early flight. I assembled it all on the baking sheet with parchment paper in the morning and stuck it in the oven and it was ready to go by the time I was! The family loved it and I loved that they got a hot breakfast and I had no pans or dishes to do on a hectic morning! I will definitely make again and again!

Oh, my, gosh! I can't believe people would actually rate a recipe low because the picture didn't match the recipe directions! People! There are 7 photos submitted by different people who put their own spin on the recipe and submitted a picture. They are all different! If you don't like the looks of one, click on it and find another! As to the recipe, I made my own crust-it is so simple and doesn't contain all the weird stuff in pre-made stuff. I did make some gravy out of the sausage I added and put it on a partially baked crust. I did it because my husband loves biscuits and gravy and thought he'd like it better that way. He said it reminded him a little of a breakfast bowl he had at a restaurant.

I'm not sure why there is a pic with a fried egg on it when the recipe calls for a soft scramble; but, it is delicious. Green onions are a must so don't make this if you don't have any! I used pizza dough from my butcher. I also modified it by placing the bacon (cooked, in strips) on the bottom and covering with the scrambled eggs and then cheddar. It's basically whatever you would normally put in a Denver omelet/sandwich but you need soft eggs to maintain moisture simce there is no sauce. Since most people put ketchup on their eggs, it probably wouldn't be a leap to use a small amount of ketchup as the 'pizza sauce' but usually ketchup is served cold on egg dishes.

I used a frozen cheese pizza instead of biscuits. It had a lighter and crispier crust. I used bacon pieces, whole eggs, and more cheese. I used parmesan but I'm quite sure any cheese will do. I will keep frozen cheese pizza in the freezer to keep it on hand for a quick delicious meal. Good for breakfast, brunch, dinner, or a late-night snack. Next time I'll add spinach. It was simply a delightful and quick late-night snack.

5 stars for the recipe, but not the amounts of ingredients. Definitely need to tone it down a bit if you're using the 9x12, an entire onion is waaaay too much, as are most of the other ingredients. Other than that, add some hash browns between the rolls and eggs (make sure they're mostly cooked first), and this recipe is phenomenal.
I thought it was great, I used sausage gravy as the first layer then the eggs topped with crumbled bacon, onion, peppers and cheese

I used grands flaky layers biscuits, separating each biscuit into 2 rounds, pre baked a few extra minutes. Then I sautéed papers and onions and added eggs to pan to scramble all together before loading on the pre baked biscuit crust.
It was good .. But a nightmare to serve .. and it was too thin to pick up had to use a fork ... ill probably make it again

We liked the idea of presenting the same old breakfast food in a new and creative way. Since my family loves anything with runny egg yolk, I did make a small change: I put scrambled egg on the biscuit dough as directed, but I also cracked 4 eggs onto the top of the pizza to bake. The runny yolks really helped prevent a pizza that was too dry. We liked it, but overall, it was just OK for us.
I didn't have any refrigerated biscuits, but I had bisquick- so I made the crust. The kids loved it!
My family really enjoyed this dish it is a really good breakfast recipe.
Loved it even though our sunny-side-up eggs were still a bit runny. will definitely make again and will try with scrambled eggs this time

Great recipe for beginners ish; I wish there were more details about how to spread the dough without so much effort- I had to pinch and spread often so there were no holes in the dough and perhaps I needed to make it thinner to get a crunchy crust, instead of biscuit consistency. Thank you for sharing.

This is the best thing ever, you can buy pizza dough in the dairy case premade, I've varied the recipe, using pepperoni, salami, bacon bits, or hamburger. Love the cheese. 
Ron Goings
Awesome! followed directions. used slightly scrambled eggs and mozzarella and chedar.
